newsitem.title: NORWAY: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND LOOKS TO REPEAT DREAM WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND LOOKS TO REPEAT DREAM WEEKEND.

text.p: Another weekend like the last one and Luc Alphand can stop dreaming about the overall World Cup title and wake up to the fact that he can win it.

"I don't want to think too much about the overall World Cup," said Alphand after posting back-to-back downhill and super-G wins last Friday and Saturday in Garmisch-Partenkirchen, Germany. "It's too much of a dream."

But with a similar effort this weekend, Alphand would lock up the World Cup downhill and super-G titles and reinforce his bid to become the first Frenchman to win the overall title since Jean-Claude Killy in 1968.
With just eight events remaining on the World Cup calendar, Alphand views Saturday's downhill and Sunday's super-G as pivotal to his quest.
On the strength of four wins the 31-year-old Frenchman leads the downhill standings with 705 points, ahead of Italy's Kristian Ghedina with 594.
With two victories in four super-G races, Alphand tops the standings in that discipline as well, 91 points clear of another Italian, Peter Runggaldier.
His successes give him a 163-point advantage over fading Norwegian all-rounder Kjetil Andre Aamodt in the battle for the coveted overall crown.
"Everything could be solved (here)," said Alphand having quickly put the disappointment of an unproductive world championships behind him.
"Leaving Garmisch ahead of Aamodt was no surprise but if I manage to keep him behind me after Norway that would be fantastic.
"I could even perhaps think about training in the giant slalom. Remember Aamodt has four times the opportunity to gather points."

While Alphand competes in only the speed events and has just four races left, Aamodt, the 1994 overall champion, is expected to ski in all eight remaining events and is capable of gathering considerable points from all of them.
Aamodt entered last weekend's races with a four-point lead but three disappointing results left him trailing.
"I have perhaps let too many opportunities slide by," said Aamodt. "I'm disgusted."
In Germany, Alphand became only the second skier in history -- after Swiss Pirmin Zurbriggen in 1987 -- to win downhill and super-G races on the same weekend.
Aamodt will not be alone in his efforts to ground the flying Frenchman.
Ghedina, who has waged a furious battle with Alphand in the downhill standings all season, has shown no signs of surrender.
Besides Runggaldier, many other skiers have designs on the super-G title with Norway's Atle Skaardal and Austria's Hermann Maier also within 100 points of Alphand.
